open_points.subject: Run recovery after an owner refusal
open_points.text: "A crash between the two leaves a run `running`, which start-up recovery advances (A14 rule 5)" and "Refusing writes one NodeExecution `refused_by_owner` for the refused element and ends the run `refused`"
open_points.question: If the process crashes after `effects` writes `refused_by_owner` but before `runs` writes run status, what persisted run status is guaranteed, and will start-up recovery process it?
options: `runs.continue_after_approval` sets the run to `running` before calling `effects`, so the crash case is always `running` and recovered by A14 rule 5.
Start-up recovery must also scan non-final runs in `awaiting_approval`/`pending` and re-derive status from trace.
`effects` must write run status `refused` in the same transaction as `refused_by_owner` (changing current ownership split).
open_points.default_guess: `runs` flips the run to `running` before delegating to `effects`, so A14 recovery of `running` runs works as written.

open_points.subject: Pre-send ownership of 'no selected instance' and other instance failures
open_points.text: "bindings.check_binding_current ... returns ... the `api_base_url`, `required_headers` and class of the instance whose name `installation.selected_instance_name` gives" and "service_invoker.prepare_request ... owns every instance failure — no selected instance, no `api_base_url`, a repeated required header"
open_points.question: Which module is responsible for detecting and reporting a missing selected instance (or missing instance fields): `bindings` during current-check, or `service_invoker` during request preparation?
options: `bindings.check_binding_current` fails with an instance-related failure and `service_invoker` is never called.
`bindings` returns a partial/nullable instance snapshot and `service_invoker` emits the first A09 rule 6 failure.
Start checks guarantee instance completeness so this cannot occur at send time.
open_points.default_guess: `bindings` returns whatever it can read (including missing parts) and `service_invoker` raises the instance failure in A09 rule 6 order.

open_points.subject: Approve/resolve check order across `runs` and `effects`
open_points.text: "Whether the run has ended is checked first by `runs` ... whether the approval is `requested` or the attempt `unknown` is then checked by `effects`"
open_points.question: What identifiers must the approve/refuse/resolve operations carry so `runs` can check run-ended first without owning approval/attempt lookup?
options: Requests include `run_id` (and element identity) plus approval/attempt reference, so `runs` can enforce first check directly.
`runs` asks `effects` to resolve approval/attempt to run before checking ended status.
`effects` performs both checks and `runs` only advances afterward.
open_points.default_guess: API requires `run_id` and element identity alongside approval/attempt id, allowing `runs` to do the first check as specified.
